# Upstream source

The Jiro entry workflow is adapted from [pstack's entry workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cursor/plugins/ccb5507cec1546dc88135c1139c811e6c59115ba/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) at revision `ccb5507cec1546dc88135c1139c811e6c59115ba`. Original upstream paths are retained only for attribution and update tracking, not as local skill or agent IDs. The upstream MIT notice is preserved in [LICENSE](skills/jiro/LICENSE).

The local `opencode-pstack` checkout at `30a3cbd1cbf83159e56d83790fc43b4493eb5fc6` supplied the entry-point reference. Its recorded upstream revision was checked against the immutable source above. No upstream installer or code was executed.

## Selection

- **Take.** One main skill selects a playbook, puts its steps first, loads companion skills as needed, favors simple code, verifies real behavior, and owns delegated work. Long runs use a decision trail. Replies remain concise and evidence-backed.
- **Adapt.** The entry ID is `jiro`, invoked as `@jiro` or through the `/jiro` command. Jiro coordinates the task, task playbooks are recipes, supporting skills are tools, and delegated workers are chefs. The registered Jiro worker ID is `chef`. Keep technical IDs and verification contracts precise. Use OpenCode tool arguments and base-directory resource resolution. Inherit the active model unless an authorized, host-confirmed override applies. Keep explicit invocation and existing user work protected.
- **Skip.** Cursor Custom Modes, `/loop`, editor plugins, model defaults, automatic PR creation, and mandatory calls to unbundled pstack skills or custom agents. Global installation and external writes require authorization. Do not treat an unattended request as blanket approval.
- **Jiro-native.** `references/recipes.md` provides compact workflows for the selected routing categories. It is not an import of pstack's individual playbooks or standalone principle skills. The command wrapper is repository-authored OpenCode configuration.

The import does not claim full parity with pstack's twenty-three playbooks. The four existing companion imports retain their own source pins. Repository maintenance remains outside skill discovery and installation. The existing cleanup playbook's unknown baseline is unchanged.

The added delegation and Microsoft Playwright ports have their own provenance records. Jiro routes to their exact skill IDs and delegates ownership of their contracts, isolation, and evidence formats rather than copying those procedures into the entry workflow. Instructions being bundled does not establish runtime availability.

The added `correct`, `teach`, and `unslop` imports also keep their own source records and MIT notices. Jiro loads them for recurring-mistake prevention, paced explanations, and writing cleanup respectively. Their slash-command wrappers are repository-authored. `teach` uses the existing bundled `how` and `why` procedures and preserves rationale confidence while applying `unslop`.

The selected `no-comments` and `principle-laziness-protocol` tools also have their own pins and provenance. Jiro loads comment review before nontrivial code review and Laziness Protocol before refactoring or adding structure.

This checkout also preserves its local six-principle router, design and reader-load skills, Effect and React guidance, reflection, cleanup, and scoped Chef worker. Shared writing and autonomy rules remain in the materialized `references/shared-rules.md`. These local companions keep their own source records and are not newly imported from the entry workflow's source pin. The merged entry uses the new native recipe book without removing those local routes or model-authorization gates.

After the user requested MCP removal, browser work defaults to the CLI or an existing project harness. MCP instructions remain opt-in for an explicit request; Jiro must not configure or re-enable that server during ordinary verification or maintenance.

OpenCode behavior follows the [V2 skills documentation](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/skills) and [commands documentation](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/commands).

# Upstream sources

Adapted from `opencode-pstack`'s `no-comments` tool and Comment Sicko reviewer. The inspected checkout records upstream revision `ccb5507cec1546dc88135c1139c811e6c59115ba`. Both files were checked against the immutable `cursor/plugins` sources:

- [`pstack/skills/no-comments/SKILL.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cursor/plugins/ccb5507cec1546dc88135c1139c811e6c59115ba/pstack/skills/no-comments/SKILL.md).
- [`pstack/agents/comment-sicko.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cursor/plugins/ccb5507cec1546dc88135c1139c811e6c59115ba/pstack/agents/comment-sicko.md).

The installed OpenCode copy was also inspected for tool-name conversion. Its machine-specific paths and global model configuration are not copied. The upstream MIT notice is preserved in [LICENSE](skills/no-comments/LICENSE).

## Selection

- **Take.** Fresh adversarial comment review, the five protected exception classes, scoped `MUST KILL` flags, parent acceptance, one rejected-report retry, root-cause fixes, approved constraint encodings, and explicit open work.
- **Adapt.** Use OpenCode's `subagent` tool with supported arguments. Use the advertised `comment-sicko` agent or a built-in `general` child with the full bundled reviewer rules. The reviewer is read-only; the parent owns accepted edits and verifies their effects. Preserve inherited models, explicit invocation, target-repository execution, and loaded-base resource resolution. Jiro calls this tool trimming the garnish.
- **Safety adaptation.** Hold uncertain protected exceptions and request evidence rather than deleting on doubt. Never discard user changes or broadly revert a checkout to retry. A correctness suppression is removed with a verified root-cause fix, not in a way that leaves broken code. Read-only requests produce proposed deletions only.
- **Skip.** Cursor Task fields, mandatory `architect` and `principle-*` dependencies, unconditional deletion of ambiguous exceptions, hardcoded global paths/model policy, and installation of a custom reviewer agent. An available `architect` is optional; otherwise `how` and a scoped design sketch establish the target shape.

`references/reviewer-prompt.md` is the adapted reviewer body. It is a bundled prompt, not an automatically registered OpenCode agent. Static packaging checks do not establish full upstream parity or live reviewer behavior.

This checkout also preserves the older installed OpenCode port's conditional integration with host-authorized pstack role settings. Ordinary Jiro review still inherits the active model. A pstack caller uses only its required role configuration and confirmed model IDs without changing user settings.

**Read-only smoke test.** The adapted rules were passed to the advertised `comment-sicko` agent for one owned JavaScript fixture. It proposed removing two narration comments, protected the SPDX license header and public API doc comment, reported no structural flags, and left the file unchanged. This covers that small classification case only. The `general` fallback, actual deletion/root-cause fixes, retry behavior, and constraint-encoding flow remain untested live.

- [pstack's Orchestrate playbook](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/ccb5507cec1546dc88135c1139c811e6c59115ba/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/orchestrate.md), specifically bounded briefs, single-writer records, evidence, context relay, and failure accounting.

Both sources were read at this immutable revision. The upstream MIT notice is preserved in [LICENSE](skills/delegate/LICENSE).

**Take.** Fresh workers by default; consolidated scope for retries; parent ownership of results; self-contained briefs with goal, scope, context, acceptance, verification, timebox, forbidden work, standing orders, and reports. Each record has one writer. Dependencies carry evidence, not just ordering.

**Adapt.** `delegate` is a new Jiro workflow extracted from those rules, not an upstream skill of the same name. Jiro's workers are chefs. Use the advertised `chef` for Jiro implementation or review, with `general` / `explore` for supported fallback and discovery roles instead of Cursor-specific dispatches. The parent stores per-attempt briefs and reports in a unique local `.delegation/<task-slug>/run-<n>/` directory, or host scratch for repository-read-only work. Reports use PASS / ISSUES / BLOCKED, with parent acceptance recorded separately. Inherit models unless user-authorized and host-confirmed. Use completion notifications rather than polling. Require a stopped predecessor before a replacement writer.

**Skip.** The upstream persona and unbundled principles; Cursor cloud placement, `/loop`, nested-coordinator assumptions, and the Bun orchestration CLI; automatic commits, pushes, PRs, merges, deploys, and broad external-action autonomy. This is bounded local delegation, not the full Orchestrate runtime.

The [delegation guide](playbook/delegation/README.md) distinguishes related upstream workflows from installed features. Runtime syntax follows the [OpenCode V2 agents guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/agents) and [skills guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/skills).

**Verification boundary.** Static checks and isolated installation cover packaging, not live fan-out, model diversity, permission enforcement, or full upstream behavioral parity.

## Take / adapt / skip

**Take:** the official command catalog, examples, task/reference structure, and
all ten reference files. References remain unchanged upstream material, not
independent execution authority. The full Apache License 2.0 is included locally;
license text and attribution are retained (LICENSE line endings are normalized
from CRLF to LF). The pinned recursive tree was complete (`truncated: false`)
and contained **no NOTICE-named files**, so there is no upstream NOTICE to copy.

**Adapt:** `SKILL.md` keeps `name: playwright-cli`, adds a scoped description,
`license: Apache-2.0`, and `metadata.opencode/autoinvoke: false`, and removes
`allowed-tools`. That field was a host-specific tool allowlist, not a permission
grant. The new OpenCode section precedes the workflow and explains loaded-base
reference resolution, target-repository execution, local-help feature checks,
unique explicit named sessions on every browser command, isolated/private
artifacts, owned cleanup, profile/attachment consent, secret handling, fresh
snapshot refs, untrusted page/WebMCP content, real-UI verification, scoped
side effects, and preservation of expected test outcomes. Session, installation,
WebMCP, annotation, and PR-attachment prose is adjusted to match those rules.

The command catalog is extracted to a supporting reference so the entry skill
stays below 500 lines. The ten original reference files remain unchanged; the
additional catalog is derived from the same pinned upstream SKILL.md.

**Skip as operational directions:** unattended global/package/browser installs,
`npm init` scaffolding, skill installation, shared/default sessions, global
cleanup or unsolicited data deletion, automatic persistent-profile/CDP/extension
use, page-tool shortcuts for UI verification, automatic PR/issue writes or
uploads, unrequested consequential actions, and test healing that weakens
expectations or silently skips failures. Unchanged examples in the skill and
references must be translated into authorized, locally supported, isolated
commands; their existence is not permission to execute them. No upstream scripts,
binaries, installers, or package configuration are imported or executed.

## Documentation pin versus package version

The commit above identifies **documentation source only**. It is not a version
constraint for `@playwright/cli`, `playwright`, `@playwright/test`, browsers, or
`gh`. Upstream `@latest`, `gh` 2.99+, `--debug=cli`, WebMCP, recording, emulation,
and configuration examples describe that source snapshot; they do not prove
availability or compatibility in a target repository. Read the installed
command's `--help` (and relevant subcommand help) before use. Do not install,
upgrade, or initialize anything solely to make these examples work.

## Verification and limitations

The import is statically checked for frontmatter, relative documentation links,
all eleven upstream skill files, unchanged reference content, full license text,
and the pinned tree's NOTICE coverage. All source was read as inert reference
material. **Live CLI behavior is untested:** no browser commands, CLI help/version
commands, package installs, browser downloads, test suites, session attachments,
recordings, or publishing commands were run for this import. OpenCode runtime
loading and the behavior of installed CLI flags/output isolation also remain
unverified. A future authorized browser task must perform its own local checks.
